questions.q: What is the first group of tables a supplier invoice's data lives in, before any accounting event is recognized?
questions.explain: The chain starts purely in Payables, before Subledger Accounting ever recognizes an accounting event.

options: A specific accounting event — a business occurrence requiring accounting, such as an invoice being validated
questions.explain: XLA_EVENTS records accounting events; a single transaction can generate more than one over its lifetime.

questions.q: What is stored in XLA_AE_HEADERS and XLA_AE_LINES?
options: The subledger's own journal entry (header and debit/credit lines), generated from an accounting event
questions.explain: XLA_AE_HEADERS and XLA_AE_LINES represent the subledger-level journal entry produced for an accounting event, before it reaches GL.

questions.q: What does XLA_DISTRIBUTION_LINKS specifically tie together?
options: A business unit and a ledger
A subledger journal line (XLA_AE_LINES) and the exact source distribution that caused it, such as a row in AP_INVOICE_DISTRIBUTIONS_ALL
questions.explain: XLA_DISTRIBUTION_LINKS is the precise link between a subledger journal line and its originating source distribution row.

questions.q: What table acts as the bridge carrying a subledger journal into GL_JE_HEADERS/GL_JE_LINES?
questions.explain: GL_IMPORT_REFERENCES is the bridge table connecting subledger accounting lines to the actual GL journal headers and lines.
